t101:
Existential risks are defined as threats to the very survival of our species. Closely related are global catastrophic risks - risks that threaten to significantly reduce the size of population over a short time span. 

The future can be vast and the welfare it holds immense, and we have the responsibility to uphold its possibility. Even small existential risk probabilities have great implications for the expected value of the future.
t102:
In times of limited resources and increasing levels of power, conflicts can become both more likely and more destructive. Therefore, it is more and more important to settle disagreements peacefully and to work together as a global whole. 

There are good prerequisites for improving our outlook on this: Techonological progress produces more and more threats but also more sustainable ways to reach a decent standard of living. Internet provides a way for a spread of globally beneficial ideas for people to support.
t103:
European Union is an example of close and continuous coordination between countries, in term negotiaation and decisionmaking. It is important for it to succeed - to motivate that kind of co-operation on a global scale as well.

European countries themselves are stronger together at the world's stage. EU should apply its joint power in negotiation tables for its countries' benefit but also for creating globally beneficial structures.
t104: My interest in climate change is motivated especially by the danger it poses to civilizational stability. Climate change can be especially harmful to agriculture. Crop failures, floods and other harmful phenomena can cause severe distress and mass displacements. This can increase the probability and severity of international conflicts, which are likely to be more and more harmful in the future.
t105:
Electrification of energy use is important for stopping climate change, because electricity can be produced with very low emission sources such as nuclear, hydro, wind and solar. 

Wind and solar are cheap to produce, but their variable production causes occassionally very high price spikes and supply issues. Making clean electicity cheap enough is important for increasing its adoption. 
I am interested in this theme especially at the level of Finland and the European Union.
t106:
It is very important that Ukraine succeeds in defending itself against Russia, both for Ukraine's survival and also for its impact on Russia's willingness to be aggressive against its neighbours in the future. Countries' contributions to Ukraine's victory also send a broader message that aggressors are punished and defenders supported. This should create a peace-building dynamic. 

I'd be interested to get a better view on if it is now more effective in the margin to exert more financial pressure against Russia or to provide support to Ukraine. And with what instruments.
t106.1: The Finnish public finances are in a poor state. The public debt is mounting in a fast pace, and the demographic transition is going to put stress on healthcare system and pension funds for decades to come.
p201:
There is a considerable yet hard to define probability for humankind's extinction, or atleast a catastrophic civilizational collapse, within our lifetime. k

I would like to create a site that allows the user to set probabilities on how likely it is for this kind of extinction event or catastropthic collapse to occur in different time periods in the future. The site then calculates the expected longevity of humankind (measured in expected years the humankind will exist or in expected human lives, for example). Results are accompanied by graphs.

The motivation behind the site is to demonstrate that even very small improvements in existential risk will pay off immensely in the long run in terms of humankind's longevity. This should motivate the user to pursue those improvements various ways in their lives.
p202: I think that we should perhaps approach existential risk probabilities more by looking at how much reducing or removing specific threats or risks would reduce the overall existential or catastrophic risk. This could reduce some issues related to how intertwined the risks are and could also lead to more policy-oriented discourse.
p204:
I'd like to write a comprehensive long text, possibly a book, on how important I view our current time.

Rough outline at the moment:
* Humankind's possibility for great future
* Current fragility of the great future
* Our great power and responsibility in guiding humanity over the fragile times
* What makes us passive despite our power and responsibility
* Some things that I think should be done, policy wise
p204.1:
The world could benefit if we encourage a system of overalapping tariff unions. Countries in an union would agree to follow some beneficial policy or abstain from some harmful policy. Anyone doing the same would be allowed to join. They would then set tariffs for non-union countries in order to encourage them to join them. 

A multitute of unions that criss-cross across countries in terms of who are partaking would make punitive tariffs a more business-as-usual practice, increasing their prevalence and effect. It could increase discussion on the global good.
p204.3:
Like many others, I am very concerned about polarization in society. Politics is a part of that, and one of its major drivers. Decreasing the polarization and tribalism in politics is therefore very important. 

I think that political parties should be more careful about increasing the political divide with their communication. They should also be lenient on embracing some centrist views in order to avoid political blocs which can lead to de facto two-party systems in which it becomes more and more effective to do politics by focusing on what the oppoonents are doing wrong than focusing on what should be done, together. 

(short text, about blog lenght)
p205.5:
If humankind is to live in a sustainable fashion, what kind of average resource use and lifestyle will it allow us? I'd like to take a look at the research on the topic.

Important to explore, because: 
- Can be used to set targets for individuals and for national policy
- Helps to identify what areas are most difficult to reach, helps to target our efforts in adopting new technologies etc. 
- A knowledge that there is a way for all the people in the world to coexist would motivate people to support global peace.
p206:
Carbon pricing is an efficient way to reduce emissions, but it causes a rather visivle cost to consumers, which often increases resistance to it. Also, the benefits of the carbon pricing (like taxation in general) in terms of government revenue are more often hidden to the public. 

I’d like to make a video that explains the efficiency of carbon pricing and its benefits as a way to create government revenue and welfare. 

Efficiency compared to other means of emission reductions is due to market mechanism automatically incentivizing emission reductions to where they are cheapest to perform, with some caveats with regards to innovation externalilities and to markets not reaching some areas that governments have a executive power over.

A portion of the video would explore the possibility of global carbon pricing and dividend, using my website https://www.globalcarbonprice.com to showcase what kind of effects the system would have with different emission progression and carbon price specifications.
p206.5:
(Written in Finnish)
Finland in undergoing a major surge in electric boilers in district heating systems. When the electricity is abundant and cheap (for example, when it is windy), the heating and heating water in district heat has practically zero emissions. 

I would like to make a website that shows the emission estimates of a minute of showering in a given area at a given time. The emission estimates would be based on information on electricity prices and the electric boiler capacities of different district heat networks and some other variabels. If district heat operators allowed access to their actual data on how heat is produced at any point in time, that could also be used for this. Emission estimates would be produced for the current day and the tomorrow. 

I believe that some environmentally conscious people would want to use this kind of information on: 
- when to take a shower
- how long to stay in shower
- how warm of a shower to take

In addition to climate, this would benefit Finnish electricity markets by decreasing the demand at peak price hours and therefore reducing those peak prices. 

This also concerns apartments under direct eletric heating. For them, it can also be used to indicate the price of showering (per minute, and depending on heating temperature, for example)
p207:
Many European countries show resistance in building new interconnectors to other countries, on account of them increasing their average electricity prices. This reluctance is harmful for the development of EU electricity market as a whole. We need more integration to make prices cheaper on average and to reduce the harms of variability in renewable energy generation. 

I wonder if it would beneficial to have a system in which countries that import electricity would pay for the exporting countries (This would, of course, be in addition to what electricity users are paying to electricity producers through grid operators responsible for the cross border electricity trade). 

This kind of system would incentivize both the exporters to build new connectors and for governments in each country to build new power generation, where possible, instead of being too reliant on imports.
p208:
Would pumped-storage hydro power be a good solution for Finland? Considering some of the following aspects:
* Economic benefits. What would be the effect on energy prices. Would the projects need government support?
* How much room is there for capacity?
* How much harm would it cause to nature and how much resources need? Compared to regular hydro and battey storage solutions.

Currently, I think it would be a good solution. However, it also needs local acceptance to get permitted.
p209:
I have made several Nightingale/radial plots for comparing countries across different topics/outcomes. Some can be seen here: https://villeseppala.wordpress.com/pictures-and-animations/

I’d like to make producing them more automatic and produce a public website for it, so that the user can select what outcome variable to look at, how to group countries (color the bars), and what year to compare to track change over time, for example. User could then download the produced graph.
p209.5:
I have uploaded some of the data visualizations I've created here: https://villeseppala.wordpress.com/pictures-and-animations/

Some of them I've updated at some points in time. Updating can be quite straigtforward if data is machine readable online and in same form as before. However, uploading and hosting the graphs takes some time too. Also, I have to do both updating and hosting separately for each graph. 

I would like to create a script that automates most of this work. So that running it would fetch the latest data, create updated graphs and host them on the site. In R, ggplot2 and quarto probably integrate quite nicely for this.  

Many of the graphs in the graph bank are outdated also in their design. Having an automation system would motivate me to redesign some of them, since I would know they would remain current in the future.
p209.55:
I've been collecting and putting together some figures on Russia's economic situation. I want to get somewhat of a full picture of it. 

My current impression is that Russia managed to keep its economy and public finances running quite well from 2022 to 2024 but the situation has worsened in 2025 and 2026. 

Link will be provided here at some point.
p209.56:
When Russia weights its options between escalation and de-escalation/peace, we must try to make the latter a more desirable option for it. As part of this, it might be wise to keep a path open for Russia to reintegrate back to western economy and trade provided that Russia ends its hostilities favourably. This reward could increase Russia's willingness to do so. 

It could also make it easier for many countries to join in on stricter sanctions if there is a clear understanding that they would be lifted when Russia ends its aggression? Sanctions are usually harmful also to the countries that set them, so the expectation that they would not need to be upheld until a certain point will lower the expected harm. 

Integrating Russia to West would also give leverage to threaten it with future sanctions. If Russia becomes more independent from West, we have less leverage on them and they have less to lose with aggressoins towards West. There is, however, a delicate balance here. Russia's integration to West, for example through energy trade, also integrates West to Russia. Dependency on Russia has made it harder for many countries to sanction it.
p209.6: Want to create a list of savings measures.
p210: Creating a homepage. Currently I'm using a wordpress base for my website at villeseppala.fi. Quarto/Markdown based website would allow more flexibility and better use of ggplot2 graphs and changes thourgh github, for example.
p211:
I'm motivated to improve this site. In addition to gaining feedback or finding funding, having the site in itself can help me finish some of my projects. Depending on how they are written, some plans for texts can also act as drafts for the text and can be continuously improved until they can be published as finalized texts. Having the plans/drafts public makes me more motivated to focus on them at that stage, since I know they can be seen and to have some kind of impact already. This increased focus increases the probability that the plans/drafts will become final texts at some points. 

I'd like to improve this site. 
In general, I will be making description texts longer or changing them as my thoughts progress. I could also add some features. If there is demand, I could modify the tools I've made with AI for tweaking/creating the site into a published version that others can use to create similar site.
s301:
Visual communication in the form of data visualizations and infographics can be a good way to grab the attention and an efficient way to convey a message ("a picture tells more than a thousand words"). This is important in a time when there is a great "competition" of people's attention and screen time. Visually appealing and concise communication is very valuable.

I've worked on data visualizations using ggplot2 in R, mostly focusing on emission statistics. 
Some examples here: https://villeseppala.wordpress.com/pictures-and-animations/
s302:
I'm interested in websites and the interactivity they allow. Compared to static communication, they allows for clickable "on-demand" content (such as these description you are reading) and an endless combination of various choices.

Previously, I've worked especially on dashboard websites using R's Shiny package. My biggest project has been https://www.globalcarbonprice.com, which allows the user to see what kind of income effect different combinations of climate targets, carbon pricing and its global redistribution would produce.
s303:
I watch a lot of youtube, and understand its possibilites in reaching new audiences and providing an efficient way to communicate your ideas. On the other hand, I feel that videos take a lot of time to produce, which fits a bit poorly with my tendency to not always follow through with my projects.  

I haven't done videos for a while, and the ones I have done have focused on showing graphs in some way. This would probably be the case in future as well but, in addition, I would include other graphical elements to visualize stuff. 
You can take a look at my videos here, they are mostly in Finnish: https://www.youtube.com/@seppalaville


Streaming, on the other hand, is quite effortless. I have sometimes streamed while working on some project. It is difficult to make this kind of thing entertaining and gain audience though, but if I managed, it could pay off through getting constant feedback.
You can take a look at my past streams here: 
https://www.youtube.com/@seppalaville/streams
I also stream to Twitch and Kick simulatenously, but they only keep the recordings for a short while: 
https://www.twitch.tv/seppalaville
https://kick.com/seppalaville
s303.5: I have an economics PhD from 2020. In my doctoral thesis, I focused heavily on empirial microeconometrics. My current interests are more related to theoretical macro- and microeconomics, which I'm not that familiar with, but my studies still give something to build on.
s304:
I've been exploring the capabilities of AI tools and want to continue it, based on my good impressions and the general AI hype.

I have mixed feelings about AI in general. I share some of the usual worries people have regarding AI's threats to society. Regarding my own skills, I'm worried that AI may weaken my understanding of how my code works, for example. 

Make it so that even if there is no edge coming fro a node (such as "social media"), it is still set by source color options and has the gradient effect. 

However, I also feel that the genie is out of the bottle, and not using AI can put you at a disadvantage on various competetitive avenues. Using AI can also better help you understand what kind of dangers it poses.
s305: I want to partake more in social media to gain audience. Also want to figure out what channels are best and most impactful for me.
